[CRLMB-3036/2024] petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.
3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have heard and considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.
5. Perusal of the material available on record revealing that the victim is a 30 years old married lady.
After going through the FIR, it is revealing that she was in relation with the petitioner and they frequently used to exchange calls.
Even from the FIR itself it is revealing that they have established physical relation on several occasions.
The allegation that some obscene material was there with the petitioner showing her in compromising situation with the petitioner falls on earth because no material has been collected in this regard.
It is also not comprehensible as to under what circumstances the intimate scene of her and the petitioner got captured.

The threat of having recording and video with the petitioner seems to be very flimsy in view of the fact that the intimate scene and voice recording between them could not have been captured and recorded until she talks with her or establishes physical relation with him.

Be that as it may, without commenting upon the merits of the case for the reasons that nothing incriminating viz., voice recording or obscene material got recovered from the petitioner, the fact that investigation from him has been completed as well as the fact that the victim is a 30 [2024:RJ-JD:12598] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-3036/2024] years old grown up lady and there is substance in the plea of defence regarding consensual relationship between the petitioner and the victim, there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.
Thus, I see no reason for further incarceration of the petitioner and deemed it suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
6. It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

7. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FRAJAND ALI),J 31-Mamta/-
